controls.label: Initial amount N0
controls.help: Changes the remaining amount N(t); it does not change the remaining fraction f or half-life t_half.

controls.label: Decay constant lambda
controls.help: Changes half-life t_half, remaining fraction f, remaining amount N(t), and the ratio t/t_half.

controls.label: Elapsed time t
controls.help: Changes remaining fraction f, remaining amount N(t), and the ratio t/t_half; half-life t_half stays fixed.

explorations.title: Halving the initial amount
explorations.instruction: Predict: will the remaining fraction change if N0 is halved? Then apply the preset, which sets n0, lambda, and t.
explorations.observe: The remaining fraction f stays at 0.6065 and half-life t_half stays at 6.931 y, while the remaining amount N(t) drops from 60.65 a.u. to 30.33 a.u.; ratio t/t_half stays at 0.721.
explorations.why: Because f = exp(-lambda t) does not contain N0, halving N0 halves N(t) = N0 * f but leaves f, t_half, and ratio unchanged.

explorations.title: Doubling the decay constant
explorations.instruction: Predict: how does doubling lambda change the remaining fraction f, the half-life t_half, and the elapsed half-lives t/t_half? Then apply the preset, which sets lambda, n0, and t.
explorations.observe: The remaining fraction f falls from 0.6065 to 0.3679, half-life t_half falls from 6.931 y to 3.466 y, remaining amount N(t) falls to 36.79 a.u., and ratio t/t_half rises from 0.721 to 1.443.
explorations.why: Both f = exp(-lambda t) and t_half = ln(2)/lambda depend inversely on lambda, so a larger lambda makes the decay faster and the half-life shorter.

invariants.name: fraction stays between zero and one
